evidence.detail: A defensible case study explains starting problems, operational interventions, measured limits, and requires explicit customer sign-off.

slides.headline: Most case studies hide the messy middle.
A buyer needs to know what changed.
slides.body: Starting with a customer logo and ending with a large percentage tells procurement nothing about operational fit.

visual.note: Source material: B2B Case Study Template

slides.headline: Reconstruct the starting problem honestly.
slides.body: Record the baseline symptoms and business consequences before the intervention, not after success.

slides.headline: Document scope without claiming magic.
slides.body: Describe timeline, responsibilities, and alternatives. Pretending there were no trade-offs destroys trust.

slides.headline: Qualitative outcomes require no inflation.
slides.body: If an improvement is an estimate, label it as such. Verified process gains are more useful than invented returns.

slides.headline: Reference willingness is not public approval.
slides.body: Seek explicit permission for names, quotations, and claims before publishing. Anonymised stories still need care.

slides.headline: Can another buyer tell where this applies?
slides.body: A defensible case study serves technical readers, procurement, and senior sponsors equally without hiding its limits.

slides.headline: An honest outcome is more useful than an invented return.
slides.body: Read the long version and access the complete structure at rachitmishra.in.

caption:
Most case studies hide the messy middle.

Writing a useful b2b case study template means documenting operational constraints rather than chasing generic marketing praise.

When you omit the starting baseline and the intervention limits, procurement committees dismiss the claims before sales even calls.

An honest outcome is more useful than an invented return. Read the full article at https://www.rachitmishra.in/2026/10/30/b2b-case-study-template/

Send this to whoever is writing your next customer case study.
